title: Quiche Florentine
subtitle: A cream and egg tart of wilted spinach and gruyere
excerpt: Soft spinach and nutmeg-scented custard in a blind-baked shortcrust shell. The filling sets firm enough to slice cleanly but stays just tender in the centre.
sourceNotes: Classic French bistro quiche, adapted from standard French culinary tradition.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked quiche whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 170C for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and serve at room temperature, or warm gently at 160C for 10 minutes.

content.text: Quiche Florentine is a French egg and cream tart filled with spinach and gruyere. The custard should set to a gentle wobble rather than a hard set. Squeeze the spinach thoroughly dry, or the filling will weep and the base will soften.
Roll the pastry to 3mm thick and line a 23cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Press into the edges, trim the overhang, and chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 190C. Line the pastry case with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper and bake for a further 5 minutes until the base looks dry and pale gold.

Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Tip into a colander and press out as much liquid as possible with the back of a spoon. Chop roughly.
Whisk the eggs and cream together in a jug. Season with the nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Scatter half the gruyere over the pastry base. Spread the spinach evenly on top, then scatter the remaining cheese over.
Pour the egg and cream mixture slowly over the filling. It should reach just below the pastry rim.
Bake for 25 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes before removing from the tin and slicing.

items.cause: The spinach was not squeezed dry enough, or the blind bake was too short.
items.fix: Press the spinach in a clean cloth before using, and bake on a preheated baking sheet for a crisper base.

items.symptom: The custard is grainy or curdled.
items.cause: The oven was too hot or the quiche was overbaked.
items.fix: Bake at no more than 190C and pull it when there is still a gentle wobble in the centre.

items.symptom: The pastry cracks when removed from the tin.
items.cause: The pastry was too thin or the tart was not rested long enough.
items.fix: Rest the quiche for at least 10 minutes before releasing the tin and sliding onto a board.
